site_article.answer_summary: Sign in at kling.ai, check your credits in the left sidebar, start from text or an image, pick 3 to 15 seconds and 720p or 1080p, and write the prompt as a shot list. A 5 second 720p clip without audio costs 30 credits on Kling VIDEO 3.0.
site_article.hero_alt: Promotional banner from Kling AI for its VIDEO 3.0 model.

paragraphs.text: How to use Kling AI to make videos comes down to three things: knowing what the free account really gives you, writing prompts the way Kling's own guide asks for, and checking the credit cost before every clip. Kling is an AI video generator from Kuaishou that turns text, images and video references into short clips with sound.

The quick version: credits are Kling's currency, a video costs credits for every second you generate, and failed generations are refunded. Kling sells credits at a standard rate of $1 for 66 credits. A 5 second clip at 720p without audio costs 30 credits on the Kling VIDEO 3.0 model, according to Kling's own user guide.
Kling AI free credits explained

Kling's credit policy lists several kinds of credits: promotional credits from events, monthly credits that come with a membership and last one month, credits from a 7 day membership, daily login credits that subscribers can claim during events, and purchased credits that stay valid for two years. When you generate, Kling spends the credits that expire soonest first.

The policy does not promise a fixed free allowance. A third-party guide from Atlas Cloud, published July 14, 2026, says the free plan gets 66 credits on the first login of each month, valid for one month, which is enough for about two 5 second clips at 720p. Treat that number as a guide, not a promise, and check your own balance.

Some features are paid only. Kling's policy names fast-track generation, 1080p video, watermark removal, master shot and video extension, and image upscaling as premium features that credits alone do not unlock. Atlas Cloud adds that free output carries a watermark and that the free queue can be too busy to accept new tasks at peak times.
To see how many credits you have, click the remaining credits number in the left sidebar on the Kling website. Do this before you start, not after a failed run.
How much a Kling AI video costs in credits

Kling's VIDEO 3.0 guide charges per second. With Native Audio on, it costs 12 credits a second at 1080p and 9 at 720p. With No Native Audio, it costs 8 credits a second at 1080p and 6 at 720p. Voice control adds 2 credits a second. So a 5 second 1080p clip with sound costs 60 credits, and the same clip with voice control costs 70.

The VIDEO 3.0 Omni model, which can also take a video as a reference, costs 16 credits a second at 1080p and 12 at 720p when you add a video input, with native audio off. Clips on both 3.0 models run from 3 to 15 seconds.
How to make your first Kling AI video

paragraphs.title: 1. Log in and check your balance
paragraphs.text: Go to kling.ai and sign in. Credits only work for logged-in users. Click the credits number in the left sidebar so you know your budget.

paragraphs.title: 2. Choose how to start
paragraphs.text: Kling VIDEO 3.0 supports text to video, image to video, and video from a start frame and an end frame. If you have a still you like, start from the image: you only describe the motion, and you waste fewer runs on a look you did not want.

paragraphs.title: 3. Pick length, resolution and audio
paragraphs.text: Set a length between 3 and 15 seconds and choose 720p or 1080p. Choose Native Audio if you want sound and speech, or No Native Audio to save credits. For a test, use 720p without audio and keep it short.

paragraphs.title: 4. Write the prompt like a shot list
paragraphs.text: Kling's guide asks you to label shots in order and describe framing and camera movement for each one. You can mark timed moments, give every line of dialogue a speaker and a tone, and ask for an accent.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: One clean shot
paragraphs.text: A single unbroken shot with no edited transitions. Slow push-in on [subject] in [place] at [time of day], soft light from the left, shallow depth of field. At the 3rd second, [subject] turns and looks at the camera.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: A short multi-shot scene
paragraphs.text:
Shot 1, wide shot of [person] walking into [place], cinematic handheld.
Shot 2, close-up of [person]'s face as they notice [thing].
[Person] (softly, in a surprised tone): [one short line of dialogue].

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: Text that must stay readable
paragraphs.text: The camera remains fixed on the word "[WORD]" printed on [object], then slowly pulls back to show [scene].

paragraphs.title: 5. Use Multi-Shot when you need cuts
paragraphs.text: In the VIDEO 3.0 input area, turn on the Multi-Shot switch and the model plans the shots itself. Then click Custom Multi-Shot to set the number of shots, how long each one runs and what happens in each.

paragraphs.title: 6. Keep a character the same across clips
paragraphs.text: Upload an image and use Bind Subject to Enhance Consistency, or build an element from 2 to 4 reference images. For a talking character, you can upload a short video to create a character element with its own voice.
What Kling 4.0 changes

Kuaishou says Kling 4.0 launched on October 15, 2026, after early access from September 30. The company says it makes clips of up to 30 seconds in one pass, accepts up to 15 reference assets and up to 10 keyframes, and can be used by AI agents through a Kling MCP and command line tool. Kuaishou did not publish 4.0 prices in that announcement, so check the cost on your own screen before you try it.
Where Kling AI falls short

Kling is strong at short, controlled shots with sound, and its prompt guide is unusually specific. The weak spot is cost. Every re-roll spends credits, 1080p and watermark removal sit behind a paid plan, and a free monthly allowance of about two short clips leaves very little room to experiment. Draft at 720p without audio, then spend on the version you keep.

Long prompts do not save a bad idea. One clear subject, one camera move and one action per shot will beat a paragraph of adjectives. If a generation fails, check your balance: Kling says failed generations are refunded.
Kling translates prompts in unsupported languages into English. Its 3.0 guide lists five supported languages for speech: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Spanish.
